name: corvath
author: Caeldeth

scripts.validate: npm run lint:check && npm run format:check && npm run typecheck && npm test

_dependenciesNote: `dependencies` holds EXACTLY what main and preload require at run time, and nothing
else. electron-builder copies every entry here into app.asar verbatim, but only main
and preload are externalized (`externalizeDepsPlugin`) -- the renderer config has no
externals, so vite already bundles every UI library into out/renderer. A renderer-only
package left here therefore ships TWICE: once compiled into the renderer bundle, once
@mui/icons-material alone was 32,259 of the asar's 38,673 entries. MUI, @emotion/*,
@fontsource/* and zustand moved to devDependencies for that reason; react/react-dom
@electron-toolkit/preload is a devDependency because the preload BUNDLES it rather
than externalizing it (see the preload config in electron.vite.config.mjs) -- a
sandboxed preload can only require electron, so leaving it external broke the bridge.
If that exclusion is ever removed, it must move back here or the app fails at boot.
Before moving anything else here, check all three: a static import in src/main or
src/preload, an `await import()` (invisible to a `from '...'` grep, and the far more
common trap), and a `createRequire(...)` call. A package that is rollup-external is
NEVER bundled, so demoting it fails at boot rather than at build.
_overridesNote: brace-expansion carries two high-severity DoS advisories (GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp,
GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg), reaching us only through dev tooling and the packaging step.
Nothing that ships to a user is affected.
SCOPED PER MAJOR ON PURPOSE. The advisory is patched WITHIN every major -- 1.1.18,
2.1.4, 5.0.9 -- so every consumer stays on the line it was written against. npm
resolves a name@range selector against the RESOLVED version, so minimatch 3.x gets a
callable default export while minimatch 10.x keeps the 5.x copy whose named `expand`
it imports.
All three lines were vulnerable here, unlike the sibling repos that only needed 1.x:
1.1.15 under @electron/asar and dir-compare, 1.1.16 under eslint, 2.1.1 under
@electron/universal and filelist, 5.0.6 under electron-builder's minimatch 10.
DO NOT collapse these into a bare `brace-expansion` override. 5.x changed its export
shape -- 1.x/2.x are `module.exports = expand`, 5.x is `module.exports = { expand,
... }` -- and minimatch 3.x does `var expand = require('brace-expansion')` then calls
it. A global override breaks EVERY minimatch 3.x consumer: eslint, @eslint/eslintrc,
eslint-plugin-react, @electron/asar, dir-compare and glob. It fails only for a pattern
CONTAINING BRACES, because minimatch 3.x short-circuits braceExpand otherwise -- so it
hides. @electron/asar and dir-compare run during packaging, where a passing build
proves nothing unless the globs happened to carry braces.
Nothing to unwind later: each selector stops matching once the last consumer pinned to
that major is gone.
GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr (2026-10) needed no floor change: each consumer range and each floor
above already allows 1.1.21 / 2.1.7 / 5.0.12, so `npm update brace-expansion` was the whole fix.
global-agent@3 -> ^4.1.3 is the one override that is not brace-expansion (GHSA-hp3w-g68c-fv3c,
8 moderate findings in one chain). The advisory is on sprintf-js and covers every version, so no
sprintf-js release fixes it. The path is electron-builder -> app-builder-lib -> @electron/get@3
-> global-agent@3 -> roarr -> sprintf-js, and electron-builder 26.17 and the 27 alpha still pin
@electron/get@3. global-agent 4 has no roarr and keeps the bootstrap export that @electron/get
calls. Build-time only: nothing here ships. Scoped to the major like the rest, so the selector
stops matching when @electron/get moves off 3.x; remove it then.
//allowScripts: npm 12 runs a dependency's install script only when this block approves it, and it skips the rest SILENTLY: a warning at the end of npm install or npm ci, exit 0 (HTOO-542). esbuild's postinstall selects its platform binary. electron-winstaller is denied: its script only selects a 7-Zip binary for Squirrel.Windows installers, and electron-builder.yml ships NSIS and portable only. fsevents is the macOS file watcher behind vite, rollup and Playwright; it is optional and installs on macOS only, so an npm ci on Windows or Linux never shows that it needs an approval. electron is absent: since Electron 42 it has no install script. The project's OWN postinstall runs install-electron instead (a no-op when the binary is there), because electron-vite dev reads the binary's path without require(), so a fresh clone could not run npm run dev ('Electron uninstall') without it (HTOO-553). Approvals are by name, never pkg@version: a pinned approval stops matching at the next bump. npm install-scripts ls reports anything new.
